messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered — INC-3456 — service=db-proxy severity=high. Symptom: pgbouncer max clients approached in us-east-1. See PD link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-3456

pagerduty: Page fired to @oncall channel — INC-3456 — database connection saturation (pgbouncer). Escalation policy: primary oncall -> pager escalation.

Alex W: ack (taking initial triage).

Priya K: on it. I see a slow ramp in write p95 latency starting ~21:03 UTC. Any recent deploys to canary?

Sam G: I deployed canary 3 at 20:56 (client lib bump for pooling). Rolling that back now.

Sam G: quick checks — pgbouncer stats snapshot:
```
SHOW POOLS;
database: writes, active: 480, waiting: 120, max_client_conn: 600
database: reads, active: 60, waiting: 2, max_client_conn: 200
```

Sam G: app logs show repeated "could not obtain connection from pool" followed by 5xx retries.

Mei Chen: Redis in same region also elevated: CLIENT LIST length ~9500, maxclients=10000. Redis CPU is okay but connections trending up.

Jordan L: initial hypothesis: new client lib leak or change in connection lifecycle creating many short-lived connections across workers -> pgbouncer reaches capacity, backlog causes downstream retries hitting redis.

Alex W: mitigation plan: 1) Pause canary (Sam) 2) Temporarily increase pgbouncer max_client_conn by ~20% (Mei) 3) Rollback client-lib change (Sam) 4) Add emergency alert to customers if errors persist.

Sam G: paused canary immediately. Starting rollback now (rolling restart of canary pods).

Mei Chen: bumping pgbouncer max_client_conn to 720 across writer pool via rolling restart with drain. Triggering on a few hosts at a time.

Sam G: rollback progress: step 1/3 completed (canary replicas scaled down).

incident-bot: PagerDuty update — INC-3456 acknowledged by Alex W at 2025-03-14T21:05:10Z.

Priya K: customer impact summary so far: spike in write 5xx errors from 21:00-21:08 UTC. Estimated affected write requests <1% of total; some customers hit transient failures. Telemetry: write_error_rate peaked at 0.9% -> currently 0.15%.

Jordan L: pulling metrics for connection slope; looks like steady +65 connections/min for ~8 minutes before plateau. This matches the drip-leak pattern.

Sam G: rollback finished, canary traffic drained, no new "could not obtain" errors in logs for the last 30s.

Mei Chen: pgbouncer connections are trending back to baseline ~2 minutes after restart. Redis client list decreasing as well.

Alex W: great. I'll remain on for handoff. Jordan, can you take ownership of RCA and postmortem? Handoff now at 21:12 UTC.

Jordan L: taking it. I'll collect logs, compare client versions, and open RCA ticket. Expected postmortem draft within 48h.

pagerduty: Incident INC-3456 status update — resolved (acknowledged by Alex W). Resolved timestamp: 2025-03-14T21:12:35Z.

Alex W: follow-ups to add to RCA: enforce connection timeout in client config, cap idle connections, add slope-based alert for connection growth (alert when slope > 50 connections/min sustained for 5m), and tighten canary rollout checks for connection metrics.

Priya K: adding runbook note: do NOT auto-scale pgbouncer automatically without drain verification; prefer temporary increase with draining and coordinate rollback if client changes suspected.

Jordan L: will open ticket RND-3456-conn-drip-canary and attach logs/traces.

Alex W: thanks everyone :thumbsup:

oncall-rotation: handoff complete — Jordan L is primary oncall for follow-up.
